extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and counsel seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO (Office of Enrollment and Discipline)
extracted.subtask_description: Petitioning the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline for reinstatement to practice before the Office under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; includes filing a petition, demonstrating compliance with applicable provisions, and obtaining the Director's determination. The page is an administrative decision granting such a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must have complied with all provisions of 37 CFR § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision states: 'Mr. Tendler asserts that he has complied with all provisions of 37 CFR § 11.58.' Compliance with the regulation is the factual predicate for consideration of reinstatement; the Director reviews asserted compliance when deciding whether reinstatement is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and receipt of a Petition for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Petition for Reinstatement must be filed and received by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (the petition in this case was received January 8, 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document begins: 'Consideration has been given to the Petition for Reinstatement of Robert K. Tendler received on January 8, 2016.' Administrative processing requires receipt of a petition for the Director to review and act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's determination of appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline determines whether reinstatement to practice before the USPTO is appropriate and may grant the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision: 'After careful review of the Petition, the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline has determined that reinstatement of Mr. Tendler to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office is appropriate. Accordingly, the Petition is hereby GRANTED.' This indicates the Director's discretionary role in evaluating petitions and issuing grants of reinstatement.
